To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“the critical oscillation amplitude, at which a resonant MEMS device suddenly changes from linear to nonlinear system behavior, is strongly dependent on the frequency spectrum and, therefore, on fabrication imperfections.”
“the critical oscillation amplitude for SPDC in scanning MEMS microrrors depends on the resonance condition and can be validated on wafer level.”
the critical amplitude of SPDC depends on the frequency of the mechanical modes of the micromirror and can thus be used to validate the resonance condition of a MEMS design on wafer level.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel MEMS sensors and actuators and the modeling of their system behavior.
a fundamental nonlinear phenomenon, which is of relevance for a broad range of MEMS applications.

the validation of the critical amplitude of spontaneous parametric down conversion (SPDC), which has been predicted in Nabholz et al. “Spontanous parametric down-conversions induced by non-degenerat three-wave mixing in an scanning MEMS micormirror” (Science Report, 9, 2018).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the critical amplitude of the micromirror strongly varies with the resonance condition and, therefore, has to be considered in the design of MEMS devices to ensure reliable operation.
we have successfully validated the critical oscillation amplitude as the critical point of the nonlinear system behavior for over 600 resonant micromirrors.
the nonlinearities in MEMS resonator systems can be modeled accurately and, thus, be used for process optimization and yield improvement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SPDC threshold is a very sensitive indicator of fabrication imperfections and thus can be used for quality assurance.
we have demonstrated a nonlinear MEMS design principle on the example of the scanning micromirror that is valid for a large number of devices on wafer level.
SPDC can be a major concern for the design and operation of resonant MEMS devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the critical amplitude is not a fixed value but depends on fabrication imperfections and has to be determined individually for each MEMS design.
the critical oscillation amplitude is a sensitive measure for the frequency spectrum and, consequently, for the MEMS design and fabrication process.
the SPDC threshold is a sensitive measure of the quality of the mechanical structure of a MEMS device and, therefore, should be considered in future product design.
